name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Rock
description: Half-kneel facing a wall with the front foot a few inches back from it. Keeping the front heel glued to the floor, drive the knee forward over the toes until it touches the wall, then rock back. Repeat slowly, letting the ankle sink a little further each rep. This is the most direct way to train dorsiflexion — the range that lets the knee travel forward in a squat. It doubles as the standard ankle measurement: slide the foot back until you find the furthest distance where the knee still touches with the heel down, and compare the toe-to-wall distance left against right. Restricted dorsiflexion is the most common lasting deficit after an ankle sprain, and it quietly limits squat depth, cossack depth and the deep resting squat.
